feed.title: Pragmatic definition of consensus for light clients

entry.title: Pragmatic definition of consensus for light clients
entry.summary:
The email discusses the efficiency and application of different cryptographic systems, specifically comparing [Raito](https://github.com/starkware-bitcoin/raito) and Floresta. Raito utilizes zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs to enhance data compression, which significantly reduces the time and bandwidth typically required for these operations. This makes it a highly effective solution in environments where efficiency is paramount. However, it's noted that despite the advantages provided by ZK systems like Raito, there remains a need for peer-to-peer (p2p) gossip mechanisms. These mechanisms are essential for disseminating information about competing forks within a network, a feature that Floresta inherently supports.
While ZK systems offer substantial improvements in data handling and network efficiency, their role is described as a "marginal enhancement" rather than a complete solution. The discussion implies that while advanced technologies like Raito provide significant benefits in specific contexts, they do not entirely replace traditional systems such as Floresta, which still play a critical role in maintaining network integrity and information flow across users.
